Two-thirds of working Russians, or 63%, support using AI in their field to some extent , a study conducted by the Russian Public Opinion Research Center revealed. According to the survey, 36% of respondents had used AI for work over the past year. This figure is higher among specialists who mainly work with documents, on a computer, reaching 58%. Experts note that 61% of respondents see potential for the use of AI in their work, including 52% who are willing to delegate some tasks to AI and only 9% who would entrust it with all of their tasks. At the same time, analysts note that most workers are not worried about AI taking over tasks performed by humans, with only a quarter of respondents, or 25%, finding it concerning.

👹 Netanyahu warned against obstructing Trump’s Gaza plan as Israel risks becoming a pariah US presidential envoy Jared Kushner has urged Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to honor his Gaza ceasefire commitments, which have been stalled by Israel’s October elections. Under the 15-point roadmap agreed with Hamas in July, Trump’s Board of Peace and the White House are pushing to implement several concrete measures, viewing the Netanyahu government’s reluctance as a major obstacle. These include: ➡️ deploying an International Stabilization Force (ISF) in Gaza ➡️ allowing construction materials to be brought in for its bases ➡️ permitting 4,000 Israeli-vetted Palestinian police recruits to train in Egypt and return to Gaza ➡️ allowing water and sanitation supplies, as well as mobile homes for displaced Palestinians, into the Gaza Strip ➡️ launching a pilot project for a Palestinian technocratic administration in southern Gaza. Speaking to New York Magazine, Kushner warned Israel against making the wrong choices: “Israel could rise from the tragedy of October 7, be much more secure and much more integrated into the world, or they can go on the current trajectory, which is to trend toward global-pariah status.” Axios reports growing frustration with Netanyahu among Trump officials, who see him as putting his political survival ahead of the peace process. In the aftermath of the October 27 elections, Netanyahu’s coalition failed to retain its majority. The Likud party’s attempts to blame the setback on an alleged Arab conspiracy failed to gain traction. Netanyahu’s political rival, Gadi Eisenkot, has already been tasked with forming a government. If successful, he could replace Netanyahu as early as next week. Eisenkot previously pledged to implement Trump’s Gaza plan within 18 months. 👍 Substack | Chat | @geopolitics_prime
